Tyson Fury has fuelled fresh injury concerns ahead of his December 11 fight against Anthony Joshua after posting a video on social media in which he appeared to have a black eye. The heavyweights will meet at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff in front of more than 70,000 fans, just over a month after the clip surfaced. The 38-year-old, who is training in Miami for the bout, recorded the video on Friday to wish his friend and sparring partner, Kevin Lerena, success against Scotland’s Scott Forrest on Saturday night. Eagle-eyed fans noticed the mark on the left side of his face. “Tyson Fury here. This is a message for my brother Kevin Lerena. Good luck on your fight, Kev. Do the business. I just want to say Tyson Fury, the ‘Gypsy King,’ is behind the ‘Lerena Army.’ If you are watching it in South Africa, head over to SuperSport,” Fury said in the clip. The video came a day after former heavyweight champion Frank Bruno said he had heard whispers that Fury was carrying an injury that could affect the fight. And having that on your head ain’t nice.” Bellew dismissed the talk as part of Fury’s usual routine. “He plays up to the camera, Frank… I do think Tyson Fury is the master of the mind games,” he said. Fury returned from retirement this year with a points win over Arslanbek Makhmudov in London in April, before stopping Poland’s Mariusz Wach in July. Fury’s father, John, has already voiced worries about the fight. In the BBC Sport series, Rivals: Fury v Joshua, recorded shortly before the bout was announced, he said, “I hope it never happens. They will get that much stick; the loser, they will not be able to cope with it.” Promoter, Eddie Hearn, disagreed, describing it as “one of the biggest sporting events, if not the biggest, sporting event Britain has ever seen.” The documentary will be available on BBC iPlayer from Tuesday, November 10.
